page.layout: One page of running text, set in one column. The right edge of the scan cuts off every line, so the text ends where the scan ends. Running head centred at top, page number at top left. Catchword "Domi-" alone at lower right.

main_text.p: ritionis exponitur. Mal. iii, 1, 2. Veniet, inquit, in templum suum Dominus, &c. Quis autem sustineat diem adventus ejus? aut quis consistat, quùm apparuerit? Et Joh[?] viii, 56. Abraham gestivit, ut videret diem meum: diem scil. nativitatis: quo assumto semine Abrahæ, Hebr. xi, 16. pa[?] tefactus est in carne, 1 Tim. iii, 16. qua magni gaudii materia, Luc. ii, 10. Si quis vero hîc diem impropriè, pro tempore, accipere malit: vis eadem locutionis, nihilo minùs permanebit: tempus nempè, quo apparuit in carne & miraculis. Sic 1 Cor. v, 5. Ut spiritus salvus sit, in die Domini quo scil. apparebit ad judicium.

Ideóque mirandum non est, si qui Scripturæ usum secuti, diem Dominicum [?] Apoc. i. de die apparitionis Domini (au[?] in carne: ut dies natalis intelligatur: au[?] in specie, quâ peculiari atque illustri visione, Johanni se patefecit, & futurum Ecclesiæ statum revelavit) interpretentur.
Resp. i. Non prorsus idem significant dies Domini, & dies Dominicus: illa appellatio generalior est, multisque modis accipi potest; hæc specialior. Arbores Jehovæ, ve[?]
The last line of the page is cut off by the scan edge; the word "Domi-" beneath it is the catchword.

page.notes: The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of all lines, so many words are incomplete (marked [?] where the cut falls mid-word). The first line reads "Mal.111,1,2" in the scan, rendered as Mal. iii, 1, 2. The printed "Quis" and "Veniet" are marked by an underline and italics as printed. The left-hand dark band and the "Digitised by Google" line are not transcribed.
